text: In this tutorial you write your first model-to-model transformation: three JjTL rules that turn the People model of the ER language into tables, columns and foreign keys.

Step one. The target metamodel, Relational, is built as in tutorial one. A Table owns its Columns through a composition. A Column has a name, a type from the SqlType enumeration and a primary key flag. A ForeignKey points at a source table and a target table.

Step two. Open the transformation, with ERD as source and Relational as target. The first rule reads: for every Entity create a Table, and copy its name. Validate, then Execute: pick the People model, keep the output name, and run. Three tables, and nothing else yet.

Step three. Attributes get a rule of their own: for every Attribute, create a Column with its name, its SQL type through a value mapping, and the primary key flag. In the Table rule, one binding fills the containment: columns equals ownedAttributes. The executor creates every target first, then resolves each attribute to the column it produced. Execute again: every table owns its columns.

Step four. The same resolution turns a Relationship into a ForeignKey. Left and right are entities; the executor replaces them with their tables, whatever the order of the rules. Execute once more, naming the output PeopleSchema: two foreign keys, pointing at tables.

Step five. Back in the editor, the Trace tab lists every rule application with its bindings, and the Output tab reports the run and any warning. Save the project: the schema is a model like any other.
